tess-support: Heads up — customer on Dedicated (eu-west) reporting a steady stream of requests routed to us-east which is causing 200–400ms p99 increases. They say affinity is local-first and weights are explicit. Repro steps attached.

mike-sre: Can you paste the failover policy config? suspecting a tie-breaker when weights resolve to equal priority.

lina-eng: Seen a similar case when client-side TTL kept sending a stale session cookie so routing kept hitting fallback pool. Could be cookie TTL vs session affinity TTL mismatch.

jia-platform: FYI our routing code picks the highest priority array index, then applies weights. If priority array is malformed (trailing comma or empty entry) it treats that priority as present but with default weight 0 -> tie behavior leans to global fallback.

tess-support: Here's what the customer sent (sanitized):
```json
{"failover": [{"region":"eu-west","weight":100},{"region":"","weight":0},{"region":"us-east","weight":0}]}
```

mike-sre: aha — empty region entry. Parser doesn't drop empty items, ends up with a priority slot that effectively nulls local-first. That matches cross-region hits.

jia-platform: Patch idea: validate and strip empty entries at config ingestion and treat zero-weight entries as explicit disables. Also add a warning when priority array contains blank region chars.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: config-validator v1.3.4 -> staging (CI passed) :rocket:

lina-eng: For immediate mitigation we suggested customer remove the empty array item and restart routing config. They did that and saw regional ratio go back to ~99% eu-west within 2 mins.

mike-sre: Follow-ups: 1) add a test case for trailing/comma-empty entries, 2) alert if post-parse active capacity deviates from expected by >10%, 3) update docs with explicit note about blank entries causing fallback.

tess-support: Closing loop with customer and filing a KB. Putting config examples in the support template so this doesn't recur. :white_check_mark:
